question: What does the term hepatitis mean?
explanation: Hepatitis simply means inflammation of the liver tissue, which can be caused by viruses or other factors. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T3#BMP116_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why are pregnant women extra vulnerable to certain strains of hepatitis?

options.A: Pregnancy permanently stops viral replication in the bloodstream
options.B: Normal pregnancy hormones completely neutralize liver enzymes
options.C: Pregnancy makes the liver more prone to severe disease
options.D: The fetus protects the maternal liver from any lasting damage

explanation: Certain viruses like Hepatitis E can cause very severe liver issues because of the unique physical stress of pregnancy. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T3#BMP116_U4_T3_h1)

question: How does the Hepatitis A virus usually spread?
explanation: Hepatitis A spreads when a person eats or drinks something contaminated with tiny amounts of infected stool. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T3#BMP116_U4_T3_h2)

question: A pregnant woman at 28 weeks gets Hepatitis A. What is the usual outcome for her liver after recovery?

options.A: Delayed progression to primary liver cancer
options.B: Complete recovery without chronic carrier state
options.C: Lifelong shedding of the virus in her stool

explanation: Hepatitis A is an acute infection that usually heals completely on its own, leaving the patient with lifelong immunity and no long-term liver trouble. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T3#BMP116_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the main way Hepatitis B passes from mother to baby during childbirth?

options.A: Transmission through casual touch in the clinic
options.B: Inhalation of respiratory droplets in the ward
options.C: Consuming poorly cooked meat during labor
options.D: Perinatal transmission from mother to baby

explanation: Babies can pick up the virus when they come into contact with maternal blood and body fluids while passing through the birth canal. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T3#BMP116_U4_T3_h3)

question: Why is it urgent to treat a newborn quickly if born to an HBsAg-positive mother?

options.A: Babies infected at birth have a very high risk of chronic disease
options.B: Maternal antibodies block all future routine vaccinations
options.C: Innate immunity in infants is too weak to clear the virus
options.D: The newborn liver grows rapidly and needs immediate protection

explanation: Giving quick treatment helps stop the virus from turning into a permanent, lifelong infection in the baby. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T3#BMP116_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which test confirms an active Hepatitis C infection after a positive screening?
explanation: This molecular test checks for the virus's genetic material in the blood to confirm an active infection. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T3#BMP116_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why is testing a newborn for Hepatitis C antibodies right after birth unreliable?

options.A: Viral particles destroy all blood cells before they can be counted
options.B: Colostrum contains substances that neutralize testing reagents
options.C: The newborn liver does not produce antibodies until school age
options.D: Maternal antibodies cross the placenta and persist in the infant

explanation: Antibodies from an infected mother stay in the baby's blood for months, which can make it look like the baby is infected when they are not. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T3#BMP116_U4_T3_h4)

question: What must be given to a newborn of an HBsAg-positive mother within 24 hours of birth?
explanation: Giving both the vaccine and the immune globulin right away gives the baby immediate and long-term defense against the virus. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T3#BMP116_U4_T3_h5)

question: A pregnant woman tests negative for Hepatitis B surface antigen at her booking visit. What is the best midwifery action?

options.A: Offer the Hepatitis B vaccine series if she is not yet immunized
options.B: Prescribe therapeutic antiviral drugs for daily pregnancy use
options.C: Isolate her from other pregnant women in the antenatal ward
options.D: Repeat the antibody screening test every single week

explanation: If she does not have the virus and is not yet vaccinated, offering the vaccine during pregnancy helps keep her safe. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T3#BMP116_U4_T3_h5)
